Theoretical hierarchical triple systems comprising three compact objects are believed to be the origin of observed high orbital speed binaries like G2928203 and M299. Inclusion of disks in these triples may be essential to explain their unique features. We investigated the dynamics of theoretical triple systems with disks through $N$-body simulations and found that disk-driven angular momentum loss causes the outer binary to shrink at a rate significantly faster than observed in the systems G2928203 and M299, particularly when the disks雙面 and lightly powered.

The study considers the universe as a finite system of coupled oscillators by modeling it on a lattice, with the cosmological term representing a fixed energy density within this framework. Utilizing lattice oscillators allows for applications of exact, numerically-based statistical mechanical solution methods. In a related experiment, researchers found that a specific type of potential leads the universe on the lattice to settle into a state exhibiting flat spacetime characteristics, with an effective negative equation-of-state parameter of -1.

This paper presents a novel variational model for image segmentation that incorporates the successes of modern image restoration methods. The proposed model leverages first-order optimization techniques, resulting in significant improvements in computational efficiency. Specifically, we introduce an innovative algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers that efficiently solves the variational model. The new model exhibits notable performance gains over existing non-variational image segmentation methods, while also ensuring a well-defined mathematical framework with a clear minimum solution. Furthermore, we illustrate the practical applicability of our approach through various image processing tasks, including image denoising, inpainting, and colorization.

Heavy spin-polarized particles, such as those observed in quasars, can interact with certain types of hypothetical particles called ultralight bosons. This interaction induces the formation of a cloud of bosons that extracts energy from the spinning particles and grows until it limits their spin. By analyzing the spins of several quasars at different distances from each other, researchers found that this boson cloud formation process can happen with masses of the bosons ranging between $10^{-16}$ and $10^{-14}$ Gev, providing valuable information about these hypothetical particles. By combining results from different pairs of quasars, the study tightens the range of masses where these hypothetical particles may exist. Furthermore, the study proposes using lighter, faster-spinning quasars to test even smaller boson masses. Lastly, it shows that studying the movement of matter around a single quasar can help determine the mass of these hypothetical particles over a very wide range.

The brain's ability to process and store vast amounts of information through complex neural connections has inspired the development of specialized computing hardware. A significant example is Intel's Loihi chip, which leverages sparse, event-based spike communications to outperform traditional computers in tasks such as classification and prediction. To verify its efficacy, researchers need to adapt high-performance algorithms to take advantage of Loihi's unique architecture, requiring new hardware-aware programming models. Testing algorithms on the actual Loihi chip can be costly and time-consuming, especially for research teams, so we developed a web-based Loihi emulator utilizing the mature neural network simulator Brian. The Web version of the emulator allows users to take advantage of existing web technologies like JavaScript and node.js for parallel processing, ensuring fast simulation times and efficient debugging.

This study  utilizes multi-wavelength data from the IRIS and IRAD telescopes to investigate the dynamic behavior of the chromosphere and transition region around the sun. Specifically, the researchers focused on a microflare event that occurred on May 19, 2017, at the sun. The data reveal the temporal evolution of key characteristics associated with two noise storm sources near the solar flaring site. The sources exhibited linked evolution in their duration, distance from the flaring region, and brightness. The results of the study reveal the existence of the noise storm sources within twisted magnetic field structures and suggest that the flaring microflare caused by the release of the stored magnetic energy caused the two structures to become increasingly tangled and cause higher emissions. The findings of the study are consistent with the concept of magnetic reconnection as the primary mechanism behind solar flares.

Traditionally, the two dimensions of an integrated magnetic optical trap have been established using planar magnets for one dimension and a single laser beam for the other. We have developed a new method to create a planar integrated trap in all two dimensions using only a planar magnetic component and a specific laser setup. We compared the characteristics of this new planar trap to a more traditional integrated trap setup and found that the new planar trap offers significant advantages, including higher peak trap frequencies, larger trap areas, and higher condensation probabilities. These results suggest that the new planar trap has a greater ability to isolate particles with high quality factors.

We investigate the gravitational attraction of a black hole on a collection of neutral particles initially contained within a specific finite region of space. The particles are assigned momenta within a limited range, and we examine how the spin of individual particles affects their movement. The use of angular momentum as a phase space variable allows us to demonstrate that in the absence of external forces, the black hole's gravitational influence is insufficient to draw in particles with substantial spin in the radial direction. However, if the initial distribution of particles is confined entirely within the equatorial plane, then black hole accretion is feasible. The inclusion of a accretion disk, required for a comprehensive model, is not addressed in this study.

An atom that initially excites itself when it moves near a micro-trap, begins to emit sustained pulses of light when its motion increases near the trap's center. As the atom continues moving, it emits consistent bursts of light surrounded by darkness. For highly energetic atoms, our model shows that the emitted light consists of distinct peaks corresponding to the atom's radial oscillations. These oscillations correlate with the emitted light peaks. Our analysis also reveals that the atom emits peaks of light that match its radial oscillation frequency. Notably, these stimuli occur outside the trap's magnetic quadrupole field influence. We also discovered that the electromagnetic emission patterns contain signs of the atom's radial and angular movements.

Recent discoveries of "blue giant" stars beyond the main sequence have emerged from the spectroscopic analysis of young stellar clusters. Specifically, in the exceptionally dense Westerlund 2 cluster at a young age of 4-5 million years, numerous such stars were identified through the OSSOS program's survey, with 13 stars found and 7 stars confirmed to have a spectral type of F or later. The observed luminosity excess is approximately 2.5 dex, and it is not a singular phenomenon, as it is found to be physically linked to the presence of circumstellar disks. In Westerlund 2, this effect is responsible for the significant portion of the luminosity deficit seen in the cluster's color-magnitude diagram. The discovery implies that "blue giants" with significant luminosity excess are found among the fainter main sequence stars. It is also noted that the presence of dense interstellar material may lead to an underestimation of the luminosity deficit. In Westerlund 2, the interstellar attenuation accounts for a substantial portion of the luminosity deficit seen in the cluster's color-magnitude diagram.

Historical documents, although visually compromised, offer invaluable insights into history and linguistics. To extract meaningful information from them, it's essential to extract a clear color image or at least remove excessive color to enhance readability and color segmentation effectiveness. To achieve this, we've developed a multi-task adversarial network that incorporates a discriminative component to evaluate the authenticity of the generated image. The network effectively removes color and enhances the background of the original document image. Experiments on the HDSR dataset demonstrate the superiority of our method over existing image improvement techniques.

The rapid growth in the amount of data contained within visual information like photographs and visual documentation has led to a significant increase in the volume of high-vis data. One form of highly visual data are identity cards, and maintaining a data base of the information contained within them would be greatly simplified if it wasn't for the need to manually extract the data. This process is time-consuming and prone to errors. This research presents an innovative solution for automatically extracting data from ID cards by combining optical character recognition (OCR) technology with NLP techniques, thus streamlining the extraction process and reducing the likelihood of mistakes. We experimented with different OCR providers and NLP models to refine our data, ultimately achieving a level of accuracy that can be used for further development in the field. The results show that our proposed method is effective and can be further optimized to improve its efficiency and reliability.

A recent innovation in vehicular ad-hoc networks is the IEEE 802.11p standard, which facilitates real-time vehicular communication by resolving clear channel assessment (CCA) issues, as well as data frame detection and channel estimation problems, through competitive electronics. However, due to multipath signal distortion, IEEE 802.11p faces significant challenges in accurate CCA performance. To mitigate this problem, researchers have proposed various solutions, including time-series analysis methods such as long short term memory (LSTM), which utilizes time series data to predict CCA status. Our proposed approach leverages the LSTM algorithm to analyze training LTE data, which is then utilized for CCA predictions, leveraging the shared technology roots of LTE and IEEE 802.11p. The RRAM technology is utilized for real-time processing, which also highlights the limitations of existing solutions in terms of power consumption, processing time, and hardware compatibility with IEEE 802.11p. Our proposed solution overcomes these constraints by utilizing the derived training data for CCA predictions, which also highlights the benefits of temporal time averaging (EEA) in enhancing the reliability of the predicted CCA status.

The process of celestial image preparation involves manually adjusting each photograph's color balance individually, a labor-intensive task that necessitates the involvement of experienced astronomers with access to specialized software. Our research proposes an automated image preparation system based on machine learning, allowing for the efficient application of necessary enhancements to large datasets. The system leverages generative adversarial networks (GANs) to develop a model capable of pinpointing specific enhancement parameters for each image. Our results demonstrate the model's ability to accurately determine the required parameters for a celestial image dataset comprising approximately 7000 newt light images. The approach significantly reduces the labor involved in image preparation, potentially saving up to 70% of the original effort and facilitating the analysis of larger sets of images.

We propose a novel neural network structure that can automatically and efficiently optimize its parameters using an updated interpretation of the Universal Approximation Theorem. The current methods for optimizing neural network parameters involve two main approaches: direct estimation from data and iterative adjustments. However, these methods come with significant drawbacks including the overfitting issue and the local minimum problem, in addition to requiring precise gradient calculations. To overcome these limitations, we present a neural network optimization method that bypasses the need for gradient calculations. The proposed method involves estimating optimal parameter values within small ranges determined by approximation error bounds, thereby requiring only boundary values of these ranges and eliminating the need for their precise calculation. The results show that this method can significantly reduce the overfitting and local minimum problems while removing the need for precise gradient calculations. The computational experiments confirm its feasibility and efficiency.

Since its inception in 1992, the European Council for the Development of Qubits has played a crucial role in advancing quantum technology through the coordination and advocacy of the community. Although the ECFA Early Career Researcher's Committee emerged in 2020, it gained official recognition at the ECFA's 2022 General Assembly. Comprising young scientists, the committee works in tandem with the ECFA to drive ECFA's objectives, while also independently initiating projects to further quantum technology's development. Over the course of 2021 and 2022, the committee organized workshops, conducted advocacy, coordinated surveys, and established a strong online presence, effectively communicating its activities through the ECFA's platform.

A type of wave propagation known as line waves has been the subject of recent research and has been demonstrated through a range of experimental setups and theoretical models across different areas of physics, including photonics. Due to line waves' inherent anti-backscattering properties, they are particularly appealing for developing integrated optical devices that minimize damage from scattering and offer enhanced robustness. This study delves into the theoretical design of an on-chip optical dual metastructure intended to create line states by utilizing the concept of topological protection. The proposed design incorporates two parallel metastructures separated by a small gap, with the ability to control the directional propagation of line waves through the adjustment of this distance. The researchers confirmed their design via computational calculations and validated it using actual physical components.

The intersection of robotics and cognitive science holds great promise for developing robust, adaptable robots capable of learning through interaction with humans and other robots. This synergy benefits both fields, with implications for robotics technology and the evolution of cognitive models. In a series of collaborative studies, a team of scholars explored various learning approaches for multi-agent settings, combining insights from cognitive science, machine learning, and reinforcement learning. This chapter summarizes these explorations and outlines future research directions.

The point estimate of the absolute deviation from the median for a variable Y is often used to measure dispersion in a dataset, particularly when the median is a more reliable indicator of central tendency than the mean. Although the mean absolute deviation is typically easier to estimate than the mean absolute error, its unbiased estimation has not been thoroughly investigated for independent and identically distributed samples. For each observation, we propose a non-negative, bias-reduced estimator of the absolute deviation from the median based on a nonparametric, strong strong minimax estimator. Under specific conditions, the bias of this new estimator converges at the rate of √n. When sample size is large, the proposed bias-reduced estimator can replace the standard biased estimator without significant loss of efficiency. A similar procedure is suggested for estimating the absolute deviation from the sample median for a Weibull distribution.

Recent research on open-domain question answering with neural models has predominantly focused on relation extraction before utilizing structured knowledge for answering questions. Nevertheless, existing methods for linking entities to structured knowledge in prior work have several limitations, including employing a binary classification approach that disregards the impact of additional entities on a particular connection. This flaw results in a models tendency to incorrectly assume the existence of relations without considering relevant details. Moreover, existing models heavily rely on hand-crafted features, ignoring the utility of utilizing learned embeddings in this context. To address these issues, we developed an innovative, non-parametric approach called a soft-based attention mechanism that determines an entity's impact on a potential relation without relying to hand-crafted features. Furthermore, we designed a novel data augmentation strategy to improve the reliability of entities in their embeddings by artificially creating difficult examples. This approach, combined with a soft-based attention mechanism, yielded substantial performance gains in relation extraction and significantly boosted the accuracy of answering questions using structured knowledge in scenarios involving ambiguous relations and related entities.

In our comprehensive analysis, we investigate how anisotropy at finite baryonic density affects the quark-gluon plasma environment's impact on quark-onium survival and destruction. By applying the quasi-particle Debye mass model, we derive and solve the quark-onium disintegration equation using the separable potential approach in an N-dimensional space. With the help of the separable potential approach, we obtain analytical solutions for the quark-onium disintegration probability and wave functions. We explore the quark-onium disintegration probability as a function of initial state momentum, binding energy, and anisotropy factor for various values of the anisotropy factor. Our results, which are visually represented in 2D and 3D graphs, are then generalized to the 4D space-time environment. With the help of an additional approximated analytical solution, we also numerically compare our results with those of the full analytical solution. We observe that as the anisotropy factor increases, the quark-onium disintegration probability also increases, and there's a corresponding decrease in the quark-onium binding energy. Our theoretical findings are grounded in the principles of high-energy physics and quantum chromodynamics.

Our investigation of Tb3RuO7 reveals the existence of collinear magnetic ordering among Ru ions below 12 K, accompanied by a unusually low transition temperature that indicates the presence of competing interactions within the material. Through our study, we identified the magnetic structure of Tb3RuO7 by incorporating multi-physics aspects, including unstabilized chiral spiral ordering resulting from the combination of rare earth ions and transition metal ions with high magnetic anisotropy. Furthermore, our analysis revealed the influence of hyperfine and uniaxial anisotropy fields on the Ru ions, leading to the emergence of a partially disordered state at higher temperatures that decays into a ordered state with a wavelength of 10 K.

This study presents an approach for processing diverse types of data that involve creating a localized functional representation of each sample. A set of local models is developed that capture the essential characteristics of each data sample within this representation. The local models are then aggregated globally to produce final predictions. A key challenge in this context is ensuring the consistency of the local models, which is addressed by introducing a novel type of model representation based on cyclic fields. The cyclic nature of the model allows it to be modulated, with a global model derived from the aggregation of the local models capable of making predictions on new data. The comprehensive design of the model and loss functions guarantees the consistency of the models at both local and global levels. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method on a range of datasets, including its application to local regression and classification, and further explores its potential for use in data with manifold structures.

The goal of semi-supervised learning is to improve a model's accuracy using a limited amount of labeled and an extensive amount of unlabeled data. This work addresses a specific variant of semi-supervised modeling called covariate shift mitigation. Cause and influence factor attributes, which represent the cause and effect on distributions, are utilized to guide a semi-supervised classifier. A novel SemiGen approach is proposed, which uses the discriminative and generative capabilities of conditional variational autoencoders while also considering the cause and influence on attributes. Experiments were conducted using UCIR performance datasets which exhibited influence and cause shifts and it was found that the proposed SemiGen approach outperformed the state-of-the-art methods.

Artificial neural networks, emulating human brain activity, have achieved remarkable success in complex tasks, but the fundamental question of how they learn remains unresolved. To gain insight into the process, this study utilizes state-of-the-art optimization techniques and large-scale numerical simulations, incorporating intricate constraints inherent to neural networks, including spatial limitations inherent to their connection patterns. Unanticipatedly, the research reveals that neural networks, in solving intricate problems, self-organize into geometric fractals. Moreover, as the complexity of the task and the size of the data increase, so does the depth of the learned patterns, causing the formation of the bifurcation BACON. Notably, this study discovers that BACON serves as a universal, inherent framework for artificial neural networks, influenced by its fundamental architecture and not affected by the complexity of the task or the amount of data. Consequently, any artificial neural network, when learning, naturally and deterministically produces BACON, which we believe offers valuable guidance in the development of neural networks and provides significant implications for spin glass models. To showcase the practical significance of our findings, the research also illustrates how BACON can be applied to neural networks aiming to decode the human brain's neural code.

Deformations of the Dehn model's T^2 element deformations are investigated.  
In the Dehn model, a T^2 element can be represented by a non-degenerate tuple (v1, v2) forming a hexagon with its dual.  
We establish a topological pair (-c1(M),-lc of(M))-inequality associated with such deformations. Here, c1(M) denotes the first Melvin characteristicelement of manifold M and lc of(M) its lattice characteristic. 
This inequality specifically leads to a strict upper limit on the lattice characteristic of M if its first Melvin characteristicelement is negative. 
Additionally, we demonstrate the existence of Teichmuller deformations in which the pair (-c1(M),lc of(M)) achieves its maximum possible value. 
Our method involves introducing a new lattice characteristic deformation linked to (-v1,-v2), particularly applicable to Dehn twists under specific conditions. 
This deformation is both structurally and conceptually independent from (-c1,lc) but reveals itself to be the element with the highest value in the ordered set defined by (-c1,lc). 
In comparison to previously published works, this deformation offers fresh insights and clarifies the relationship between (-c1,lc) and (-v1,-v2).

Hadronised jets in hadron colliders originate from multiple sources, including Quantum Chromodynamics processes and weak force-mediated decays of heavy particles.  Jet classification is an essential element of high-energy physics analysis to identify new physics beyond the Standard Model.  With the advent of deep learning, jet classification reaches unprecedented levels of accuracy by leveraging a multitude of features and combining them effectively.  Despite this advancement, understanding the contributions of individual features and interpreting the results of classification remains a challenge.  In this study, an innovative jet classifier is designed using relevant moment-based features and a deep learning model that incorporates the Layer-wise Relevance Analysis to provide clear and interpretable classifications.  When applied to top quark classification at proton-proton collisions, the newly developed solution surpasses the performance of existing solutions at a 1% loss in efficiency.  It successfully identifies the impact of each jet component at a particle physics level, quantifies the significance of each deep learning layer in classification, and reveals how particle physics concepts behave within the jet when relevant dissemination layers are removed.  Additionally, a comparison is conducted between a jet composition metric introduced here and the Nambu-Jost-Lowie model to describe jet hadronisation processes.

This study introduces degenerate r-connected Stirling numbers as a generalization of well-known Stirling numbers and explores their properties through unique recursive relationships and compact degenerate operator expressions. Furthermore, the study establishes theorems and identifies connections between different Stirling numbers.

Researchers have further developed the method of creating core sets of symmetry induced representations for Schrodinger equation Hamiltonians using local symmetry elements. These Hamiltonians are designed to adhere to the constraints set by the lattice periodicity theorem. The key to constructing these Hamiltonians lies in the double group theory for spin-orbit coupled systems. From a foundational set of local symmetry elements, a minimal collection can be identified to induce the entire set. The strategy for inducing core sets involves initially identifying the irreducible sets from the full group's local symmetry elements, followed by a systematic traversal down the hierarchy of subgroups formed by a type of local symmetry called ash symmetry operations. The ash operations serve to reduce the core sets by appending ash operators to the irreducible non-ash symmetry operators. The methodology for constructing these core sets for both ordinary and double ash groups for single particle and double particle equations is described, with a demonstration provided using the lattice of a cubic system.

Sukhanov and the author have been exploring the connection between Killing vector fields and momentum operators in configuration space, leading to the identification of specific conditions under which Killing vector fields can represent momentum operators. They found that this requirement can only be met when the manifold's topology is simple and lacks knots. For manifolds with complex topologies, new momentum operator criteria were proposed, which allow for momentum conservation in certain reactions. These conditions translate into specific constraints on the momentum vector for particles undergoing change, stating that the sum of the momentum parameters multiplied by the winding vectors of the worldlines must result in a zero for all possible configurations. This momentum conservation principle can be applied in scenarios such as the ANS accelerator, where it may help in analyzing data and simplifying the process of determining the best fit models.

The Hubbard model, widely used as a testing ground for quantum many-body systems, suffers from a significant challenge known as the "sign problem." This problem poses a major barrier when using Monte Carlo methods due to the occurrence of negative configurations. We've successfully applied a novel technique, the Hubbard sign dilemma (HSD), to mitigate this problem by redefining the stochastic sampling process using complex weights. The HSD relies on a neural network that can utilize any differentiable function of real or complex arguments. Here, we employ the Rectified Sigmoidmap in the real domain, its complex extension being the Real-Exponentialmap. By leveraging the properties of the Real-Exponentialmap, we successfully transform a intractable Monte Carlo estimator into a viable one, thus resolving the sign problem for the Hubbard model at zero temperature with mid-filling and even filling configurations, where previous methods failed. Our research indicates that hopping phases no longer cause any measurable impact on estimates after the implementation of the HSD, with notable improvements seen in accurate estimations of double occupancy. These outcomes are comparable to those obtained through variational methods utilizing neural networks.

A composite Higgs model is proposed with global flavor symmetries, where a chiral representation of the symmetry group is broken into a subgroup. This concept novelly incorporates global symmetry parts within the composite Higgs sector, introducing multiple Higgs degrees of freedom. We examine a model with $SU(4) \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_B$ symmetry where global $SU(4)$ is broken to $U(4)$. We demonstrate that the broken generators' Goldstone bosons and part of the 15-plet from the 5-plet decomposition can be unified into a single $SU(2)_L$ doublet, consistent with the Standard Model's Higgs sector while substantially suppressing corrections from composite physics. This framework offers a natural explanation for several Standard Model puzzles such as the hierarchy and flavor problems, the Veltman mass fine-tuning issue, and the muon anomalous magnetic moment problem. Additionally, we analyze the model's phenomenology and its constraints from the LHC and flavor experiments, showing that the model addresses the muon anomalous magnetic moment problem without severely conflicting with other data.

Research into how sensory awareness changes in VR has mainly been based on how people
perceive things externally.  This report focuses on exploring the internal sense of
bodily awareness within the context of VR.  Experiments were conducted where subjects
wore a strobe and an haptic device while undergoing a 20-minute session of sensory
deprivation.  Afterward, their internal and external sensory awareness was tested using
standardized psychological tests.  Results showed that subjects exposed to specific VR
conditions rated their internal and external sensory awareness as more distinct and
separated from each other.  The report also discusses potential applications of these
findings to VR-based therapies.

Uncovering languages with limited textual data and existing on dictionaries, like Assamese, pose a challenge for BMLF's text generation models. Despite being pre-trained on Assamese Wikipedia and Assamese recipes, the languages' primary datasets are insufficient to yield effective results in text generation tasks. To overcome this limitation, we propose adding Assamese to the BMLF's source languages and incorporating an auxiliary language data source to boost its performance on text generation tasks.

Our research focuses on a theoretical developmental model of a dual stellar system, composed of two stars orbiting each other, which themselves may be binary systems. As a single massive core begins to collapse, it starts forming these stars, causing its total mass to increase as it accretes surrounding material. This material formation process is influenced by the core's rotation and the generation of jets, potentially responsible for clearing out circumstellar disks within individual systems and early stages of planet formation. As mass accumulates in each forming star, so does its angular momentum, prompting the core to break up into smaller components to preserve the conserved total angular momentum of the initially collapsing cloud. As a result, masses are transferred to individual system members through various mechanisms including mass ejections through jets or stable discs. As these individual system members continue to form, they may themselves develop discs, which are essential for the eventual emergence of planetary bodies or protoplanetary discs.

This research introduces M-ar-Ketand Fast Procrustes Approach (M-ar-K-FPA), a novel dimension reduction technique of independent component analysis. It integrates the practical aspects of the tactilely corrected ICA's temporal convolutional model with the efficiency of FastAP A in the context of proton column convolutional mixtures. It achieves this by utilizing the temporal convolutional model to extract basic sound sources and the tactilely corrected ICA to address the mismatch between predicted and actual data. Additionally, the proposed method leverages the FastAP A's efficiency for optimized performance. Furthermore, M-ar-K-FPA employs FastAP A to expedite the source separation process. Experimental outcomes from diverse data sets have validated the efficacy of M-ar-K-FPA in generating refined low-dimensional representations. It has also expedited the source separation process while producing representations comparable to the tactilely corrected ICA.

This research paper builds upon the foundational work of Forster et al. (2019) in demonstrating the limitations of polynomial calculus proofs. It refines and generalizes their approach by introducing a graph-theoretical interpretation that clarifies the underlying structure of polynomial calculus. This new perspective reveals that the failure of polynomial calculus proofs to differentiate certain structures in demonstration complexity is inherently tied to the first-order logic's limitations, providing a more direct connection between these two concepts. This study also introduces a novel concept known as first-order Polynomial Calculus, which we show is equivalent to first-order logic enhanced with counting capabilities. This finding generalizes a previously studied system from demonstration complexity to a more abstract setting.

A reduced commutative ring is defined as having a zero product for distinct factors, which relates to the concept of strong commutativity in additive groups. This paper delves into the classification of $\sigma$-primitive rings, the largest class containing strong commutative rings. A novel infinite family of $\sigma$-primitive rings is introduced, involving a subset of additive groups, $G_{p,q}$, from Exexian's and Chein's work. Conditions for $\sigma$-primitive rings among these groups are established and demonstrated, particularly revealing that the intersection of prime orders leads to $\sigma$-primitive rings and explaining previously known results in the process.

In programming, it is impossible to directly check the truth of certain logical statements known as L$\exists^2$ assertions. The issue arises because of the existence of the real number system, which has an uncountable number of elements. As a result, the set of program outputs is uncountable, making it unmanageable to verify the truth of these assertions. Nevertheless, the program inputs are typically discrete and can be enumerated from a finite set, allowing us to differentiate between the statements verifiable by input and those verifiable by output. In this paper, we focus on the former case and propose a method to catalog the unique characteristics of these statements based on their dependencies on the specified inputs and suggestions.

Using social media platforms with geographic locations, such as Twitter, enables journalists and researchers to track breaking news and emerging trends geographically and temporally. While existing algorithms address specific scenarios, there's a need for a comprehensive approach that can identify ongoing events in real-time, forecasting their future locations and timelines. To achieve this, we present ProactiveEvent, a machine learning-based system that identifies events predicting further events, their temporal patterns, and geographic distributions. Leveraging a deep learning autoencoder, ProactiveEvent learns social media posting patterns, flagging anomalies that indicate new events. A clustering-based greedy algorithm then groups related data, identifying mother events and their occurrences. An adaptive time-series predictor determines each occurrence's end date. Finally, we demonstrate our system using analysis of Twitter data related to the Gezi Park protests in Turkey.

The cross-correlation of the CMB and galaxy surveys allows researchers to study the integrated effects of cosmological structure growth, providing valuable insights into the evolution of the universe. This integration is represented through the lens-space bispectrum, which captures a wide range of information from different sources, including galactic non-linear growth and cosmological feature modulation. Analyzing the B-modes of the bispectrum is particularly challenging due to its complex and high-dimensional nature. This research presents a technique based on the angular decomposition of the B-mode phase, which examines how non-linear growth affects CMB fluctuations by altering the CBB coefficient. This approach is capable of detecting subtle changes and provides a framework for understanding the underlying dynamics at play.

We analyze Bayesian estimations in relation to their counterparts that guarantee resistance against adversarial manipulations. By examining the relationship between the two estimators, we find that the adversarial resilience of the Bayesian estimations is guaranteed when specific convex properties are met for a given model class. Focusing on maximum likelihood estimation, we identify scenarios where this estimator is certifiably resilient. We also investigate the trade-offs between its accuracy and its resistance to manipulation. Furthermore, we develop new techniques to assess the robust risk of this estimator and these methods are applied to specific scenarios, including binary classification with both multinomial and伯努利 models.

The rapid spread of digital misinformation poses significant threats to public health and safety during health crises like the COVID-19 pandemic. As a result, researchers have become increasingly focused on analyzing and tracking the dissemination of false information on social media. In this context, we examine the propagation mechanisms and the impact of digital misinformation in China's largest short-video platform, where over 500 million users consume over three hours of video content per day. We collect a unique dataset of over 1.5 million videos and discuss how it contributes to understanding the underlying dissemination patterns of social media information. From an analytical perspective, we identify and discuss the types of digital content, dissemination channels, temporal distribution, and spreading mechanisms at play. In terms of content, we uncover the dominant categories of content and their underlying dissemination mechanisms, along with the underlying patterns within each category. In terms of dissemination mechanisms, we distinguish between disseminators who share content they created and those who share content created by others, and we compare their underlying dissemination patterns. Finally, we investigate the impact of digital content on disseminators and the content creators, and the underlying spreading mechanisms at play, and discuss the implications of our findings.

This study delves into the impact of reducing the spectral dimensionality of hyper-spectral images on their classification accuracy. We utilized a comprehensive dataset of 200 images, spanning 13 diverse applications, to examine this effect in detail. By doing so, we generated an "HSC SDM" curve, illustrating the relationship between spectral dimensionality and classification performance. The results reveal that both supervised and unsupervised approaches exhibit peaks in performance at specific spectral dimensionality levels, which vary by task. Notably, our findings show that preserving spectral information is crucial for accurate hyperspectral classification, counter to the common practice of removing redundant information. We provide in-depth analysis and recommendations to guide researchers in selecting appropriate image sets for their respective tasks.

This paper explores the theoretical foundation of reasoning in non-monotonic logic, relying on an updated framework that integrates rule priorities and exceptions, and is built upon a modified Gamma-logic framework. It demonstrates a crucial reduction from this refined framework to Provisable Logic with the development of a new formal system, called Provisable Logic, and proves the logic's consistency by establishing a correspondence relationship between the underlying models of both logics.

Recent breakthroughs in quantum computing have enabled the application of variational quantum eigensolvers to accurately calculate small molecular displacements, including the unique characteristics of amide protons in proteins. Advances in computational efficiency have facilitated the integration of quantum computing results with traditional protein structure analysis methods by analyzing vast numbers of possible structures. Through the use of high-quality synthetic data as a benchmark, the quantum-based approach has demonstrated the ability to accurately determine the displacements of amide protons and enhance the framework of protein structure validation. As the capabilities of quantum computing continue to evolve, this innovative technology promises to revolutionize the field of structural biology and open up new research possibilities.

Convolutional Neural Networks are now a standard approach for solving computer vision tasks. While research has focused on exploring the efficacy of diverse network architectures and training methods, relatively little work has been done on the impact of different loss functions on performance. This study delves into the effect of various loss functions on classification accuracy, providing an in-depth analysis of their implications and offering a comprehensive reference guide for loss function selection.

Describing complex interacting systems, such as those found in quantum many-body systems and parapsychology, is a significant challenge due to the difficulty in accurately calculating their properties. Parquet theory is a sophisticated diagrammatic approach that aims to address this difficulty by incorporating all relevant infinite sets of diagrammatic contributions. In our research, we have developed a novel Hamiltonian framework to derive the parquet self-energy self-consistent equation, providing a clearer understanding of its structure and development.

The current study employs first-principles calculations to investigate excitation-induced condensation in a 2D material, titanium diselenide. A temperature-dependent model is developed to model thermal effects on the lattice structure, and a k-dependent scattering mechanism is implemented to replicate experimental conditions. With these models in place, we are able to reproduce the characteristics of experimental data and uncover underlying mechanisms of phase transitions. Our results also reveal that beyond the immediate impact of excitation, stranger condensation may arise from momentum transfers originating from carrier diffusion prior to carrier recombination.

Effective security management for large-scale community events relies on efficient resource allocation, particularly dispatchers who coordinate security personnel. Community events often employ text-based reporting systems allowing them to gather real-time incident information, enabling smarter resource distribution by analyzing the submitted texts. However, there is a lack of research exploring the textual interactions between stakeholders in these systems, particularly the insights provided by dispatchers using existing reporting systems. In our investigation, we analyzed the textual contributions of dispatchers using the event security reporting system developed for Taipei's annual Night Festival. Through quantitative and qualitative methods, we examined the dispatchers' textual inputs, revealing their professional expertise and commitment to enhancing the system's utility for future events. Our study highlights the need for textual analysis of stakeholder interactions to bridge the technological shortcoming in text-based reporting systems' current implementations.

This research examines the influence of nematicity on the paramagnetic response of a superconductor with d-wave symmetry. A crucial finding is that nematic deformation impacts the energy of certain single-particle excitations near a specific point on the Fermi surface, while the response near another point remains unaffected. In consequence, the magnetic response exhibits anisotropy aligned with the nematic direction in three-dimensional space. Furthermore, we have derived an expression for the anisotropy ratio of the susceptibility in terms of nematic parameters and temperature. Anisotropy is observed not only in three-dimensional space but also in two-dimensional planes oriented perpendicularly to the z-axis. We derived that the anisotropy in this plane follows a simple functional form involving the ratio of the square of this deformation to the square of the Fermi velocity. Anisotropy is also observed in the susceptibility of two-dimensional superconductors, where our calculations yield expressions for the anisotropy in terms of specific material properties for both thin films and quasicrystals with specific fixed values for Fermi velocities. Anisotropy is anticipated in experimental settings, particularly in MgB2 and superconducting thin films grown on nematic substrates where strain is present. Anisotropy in the paramagnetic response may also be evident in other nematic superconductors such as LaFeAsO$_{1-x}$ and BiSrCuO nematic superconductors under specific conditions. An

Engaged learning is essential for education in the 21st century. This paper applies the concept of a minimax strategy to create an learning environment that consistently delivers value for both educators and students. That environment is engaged education. A review of existing research on classroom minimax is also included.

This research examines the changes in musical composition from 1830 to 2020, examining how the musical language used by composers has been evolving over time and the extent of these changes affecting individual pieces of music. By analyzing over 600,000 songs by more than 15,000 composers, our results show that younger composers tend to utilize more of the musical elements available to them, similar to the patterns observed in linguistic languages. Furthermore, our data reveals that the complexity of individual musical works remains relatively stable over time, suggesting that composers are generally limited to using around 50-60% of the musical elements at their disposal, a phenomenon often referred to as the 'bounded efficiency' principle. Notably, this study provides the most comprehensive data on musical composition to date, providing valuable insights into the composition process and the creative decisions made by composers.

A thorough examination of the convergence properties of the mean squared error associated with a multivariate mean estimation problem is conducted. This problem is approached using an asymptotic framework based on increasing sample sizes, which are obtained through independent experiments. A specific estimation procedure, which is rooted in both the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem, exhibits asymptotic normality with variance scaling inversely with the corresponding sample sizes. This phenomenon gives rise to a novel variance behavior characterized by harmonic mean-like dynamics. Empirical evidence suggests that such behavior is applicable in the context of sampling methods involving repeated reinforcement and exploration.

In 2006, the International Conference on the Foundations of Artificial Creativity was held in Amsterdam and marked the first instance of an AI conference specifically dedicated to creating content, rather than the more conventional cognitive-based approaches. This gathering brought together researchers exploring various disciplines including computational design, music, performance, and music therapy. This paper outlines the rationale behind organizing this conference and illuminates the diversity of contributions presented at the event through examples of work presented within various conference proceedings. A notable compilation from the conference includes proceedings from icaf.aic.org

Reward learning in complex real-world applications often depends on expert knowledge, but these experts struggle with the increasing complexity of the problems.  The problem complexity causes bottlenecks in the learning process, where experts become overwhelmed.  To address this issue, we focus on an efficient learning approach for graph-structured data, where graph samples are presented to experts in clustered form, and experts compare the entire groups to identify their relative quality.  The efficiency of this ranking-based method is enhanced by exploiting human visual capabilities, allowing individuals to process and identify patterns across multiple samples simultaneously.  The proposed method leverages geometric properties inherent in the graphs to create hidden representations that capture the rankings, and we prove that our geometric embedding can accurately reflect the linearly separable ranking data provided by the experts.  The proposed method offers a more efficient platform for graph-structured learning tasks, and we observe significant improvements over current learning benchmarks through empirical validation.

A vector space E is over a field R's Smyth powerspace, denoted as ${\mathcal P}_S(R)$, if it satisfies the equation ${\mathcal P}_S(R)\cong R\times V$ through some R-module structure of the space.
We investigate under what conditions this property holds for the ring R. Our study reveals that the property is always true for a field's case and we establish a sufficient condition for it to hold for any commutative ring.
Our findings have broader implications in axiomatic mathematics and order-theoretic semantics.

We investigate the capabilities and constraints of two-dimensional perfect liquids to aimed vortex loops the moment they form, using the vortex loop equation to model their creation. It is found that the vortex loop equation can be resolved only if the loops move at a specific maximal velocity, and this same condition was previously established for classical and quantum point particles. Consequently, the same issue arises for vortex rings in a 2D perfect liquid, and we explore the implications of requiring optimal velocities in these systems. To set the context, we review the concepts of multiplicity and optimality that are essential to our analysis, and then focus on vortex loops, examining their degree of optimality and multiplicity. The concept of optimal velocity becomes more complex for vortex loops due to the presence of multiple maximal velocities, and we define a nuanced notion of optimal velocity for these systems. The issue of non-uniqueness of solutions to the vortex loop equation is addressed, particularly for vortex rings where up to countably many solutions may exist, and the dependence of these solutions on the initial conditions is examined. The implications of the potential multiplicity of vortex ring solutions on observations are discussed, and a pertinent example illustrating how different vortex ring solutions can lead to the same observable outcomes is provided.

A primary objective for climate models is to produce accurate stochastic forecasts of climate variables, which support statistical downscaling.  Current models, however, often fail to produce varied forecasts, despite the potential for these irregular forecasts to be improved by post-processing techniques known as statistical downscalers.  In this study, a modified algorithm called Standardized Enhanced Inverse Likelihood weighting (SEIL) is presented, incorporating the utilization of neural networks to improve ensemble forecasts.  By integrating the concepts of novel ensemble forecasting and regression analysis, the SEIL method can produce enhanced probabilistic forecasts of climate variables.  Using model outputs from the Community Earth System Model, the SEIL procedure is applied to ensemble weather forecasts of surface temperature and precipitation in the US, demonstrating improved accuracy and reliability.  SEIL is a versatile technique, applicable to any ensemble-based climate model, and can be effectively used to generate reliable probabilistic forecasts of surface weather.

A comprehensive review of experimental evidence for tau lepton CPT invariance anomalies is provided, focusing on both standard and non-standard scenarios. Unlike CPT invariant cases, CPT violating cases have distinct particle and antiparticle masses with unequal energies and momenta. This leads to an imbalance in available phase space, influencing decay ratios and affecting decay product energy spectra, particularly for decays with polarized parent particles like those in a three-body configuration. This review focuses on charged and neutral modes of tau lepton decays from e+e- annihilation experiments, with particular emphasis on B meson decays to tau lepton pairs and neutrino/dui pairs, offering guidance for analysis and interpretation of upcoming lattice QCD results on these processes.

Two spherical tanks of water in rotation, subjected to differential speeds, were analyzed to model atmospheric circulation. This was done by comparing the rotation rates of the upper and lower layers to those of models developed by Reade and by Glauditz, assessing the impact of two key variables: the rate of angular velocity change with respect to height and the horizontal velocity variation. As a result of this study, it was observed that the patterns of wave movement were unaffected by the rate of angular velocity change, but the vertical variations in this parameter had significant implications. It was also noted that the rate of angular velocity change with respect to height played a crucial role, which aligns with both numerical simulations and theoretical predictions by Geometre. Upon analyzing the vertical variations in the rate of angular velocity change, it was discovered that the rate of angular velocity change with respect to height contributed to the vertical movement of waves. This was found to support the theoretical predictions of Geometre.

This research focuses on Bayesian inference for extreme value analysis, specifically examining the threshold parameter and a parameter related to a Weibull domain of attraction, based on a threshold that is chosen in a practical way and above the data set. The chosen likelihood function can be mapped to the study of independent Poisson process measures, which allows the application of Markov chain Monte Carlo methods to sample from the posterior distribution of the parameters. These methods were implemented in the 'extremes' package in R, which we discuss in a separate paper. Our work builds on previous Bayesian approaches in the field, which typically utilize the generalized Pareto distribution or a model derived from the Fisher-Tippett theorem, which we show is equivalent to the current approach.

A common assumption in reinforcement learning is that the training environment is unaltered and consistent. In reality, especially in offline RL scenarios with a fixed dataset, this assumption is frequently breached due to various forms of subtle manipulation in the environment. As a result, policies trained under such circumstances are often compromised. According to a widely accepted theory, RL systems受 a fundamental bias known as the exploration-exploitation dilemma, which drives exploration towards unfamiliar behaviors. Exploitation biases policies towards established behaviors found in the data. This concept has been used to explain many environmental changes and their effects on RL. However, not all modifications have the same impact, and understanding the nature of these changes is crucial for developing robust policies. We introduce the framework of corruption-resilient offline RL, which aims to create environments that are less susceptible to manipulation and maintain accurate representations despite being contaminated with anomalous data. As a starting point, we propose a novel measure and theoretical framework to identify environmentally induced biases in offline RL. We establish a comprehensive taxonomy of environmental modifications, their induced biases, and the resulting shifts in the learning dynamics. We argue that effective offline RL should prioritize finding the cleanest subsets of the data to represent the true exploration-exploitation trade-off accurately. We present Concrete, a practical approach that utilizes our insights to create such purified datasets effectively. Consequently, policies trained using our method are more robust and exhibit a significant improvement in performance, reaching a 10x enhancement in specific cases.

This research focuses on analyzing the relative entropy of one-dimensional heat conduction with variable boundary conditions, leading to a key concept, logarithmic curvature, which determines the maximum rate of change for Entropy-Energy inequalities over time. An optimal, positively-inferable lower limit for this variable has been found for pure Newton's law of heat conduction, while a broader class of non-linear processes allows for a wider range of limits. This study also finds the optimal Sharpe ratio for estimating the initial state of 1-D systems through entropy-based observables, when boundaries vary.

This research explores the question of how to define and recognize texts that are outside the scope of a model's training data. We propose a new framework for understanding out-of-distribution (OOD) texts, which are defined by their deviation from a particular pattern or category of one-tok sentences. We provide examples of distinct OOD text categories, such as altered word order, missing, non-related sentences, and briefly explain the source of these categories. We propose a system for categorizing OOD texts by identifying multiple OOD categories, and demonstrate its effectiveness on four established detection benchmarks. The model shows improved performance by achieving better OOD identification results and highlighting the relationship between o anisotropy, detection, and classification capabilities. We propose a new approach for OOD text classification, which is based on a combination of one-tok sentence representation and cluster analysis. The method successfully identifies one types of sentences, even when these types are not present in the model's training data, and outperforms other models on four established detection benchmarks. The study reveals a relationship between the number of one-tok sentences, and a potential impact on one types of sentences, and one types of sentences, and the ability of a model to adapt to changing one types of sentences. We provide codes for our model at https://github.com/ajkay/OOD-Category-Classification.

In the realm of nanotechnology, tiny machines known as molecular engines are being explored to solve fundamental problems in thermodynamics and solve complex optimization issues through the joint principles of quantum mechanics and thermodynamics. This novel field, called quantum thermodynamics, leverages the inherent tunneling dynamics of quantum systems to drive tiny machines. This work delves into the intricate movement of molecules within Brownian engines, specifically those powered by quantum tunneling electronic systems, highlighting the pivotal role of electron flow and bond vibrations. By incorporating electronic tunneling rates into the dynamics of these molecules, researchers can gain a deeper understanding of the movement of these molecules, ultimately paving the way for the design of advanced molecular devices harnessed by quantum tunneling electronic systems.

The Unidirectional Resynchronizability problem for term transducers is a theoretical challenge that focuses on determining if a specific transducer can be reconfigured to align with specific output word lengths, and if so, under what conditions. We've successfully solved this problem with an efficient algorithm that operates within a time complexity of exponential length and polynomial evaluation, significantly advancing previous research. Our solution also leads to new applications in the areas of equivalence and adjunction within the context of unidirectional transducers.

This research paper proposes an efficient method for determining the coefficients of a polynomial, given its evaluations at the roots of a specific cyclotomic polynomial. Although related algorithms already exist for seamless and dual transformations between a polynomial's coefficients and its values at these roots, there has been a lack of research on rapidly computing one set from the other. This study aims to bridge this gap by introducing new theorems and algorithms that enable the calculation of either set from the other in a time complexity of O(nlog^2n).

The discovery of ultra-cool companions orbiting stars has shed light on the long-standing debate over the boundary between stellar and planetary objects. This study presents a novel approach to determining the properties of distant objects at an age of approximately 1.1 billion years, using data collected by the James Webb Space Telescope for the brown dwarf companion of T-dwarf 229, system known as T 229 AB. Notably, 229B is the first known object to bridge the gap between the stellar and planetary spectrum at this age. By applying machine learning to analyze data collected by T 229 AB, researchers found that 229B's surface gravity is 5.11 with a 95% confidence interval, 229's estimated age of 1.1 billion years aligns with previous findings. This discovery provides valuable insights into 229B's properties and the evolutionary trends at this age. This discovery also highlights the power of machine learning in analyzing data collected by T 229, with high precision estimates for 229's properties using diverse spectral libraries. This discovery provides a foundation for further spectral feature analysis and a deeper understanding of 229's atmospheric composition. This discovery highlights the potential of data collected by T 229, with high precision estimates for 229's properties using novel retrieval techniques.
